relations.note: Signý is Óðinn’s great-great-granddaughter through Sigi, Rerir, and Vǫlsungr.

relations.myth: Sword planted in Barnstokkr at Signý’s wedding
relations.note: Disguised, Óðinn plants the sword that provokes conflict between Sigmundr and Siggeirr.
Sigi is Signý’s great-grandfather in the Völsung genealogy.
Rerir is Signý’s paternal grandfather.
The giant Hímnir is Signý’s maternal grandfather through Hljóð.
Signý is Vǫlsungr’s daughter and one of his two eldest twins.
Vǫlsungr accepts Siggeirr’s proposal despite Signý’s foreboding and enforces the pledged marriage.

relations.myth: Signý warns the Völsungs of Siggeirr’s ambush
relations.note: Vǫlsungr rejects Signý’s warning to retreat and orders her back to her husband.
Signý is the daughter of Vǫlsungr and Hljóð.
Signý and Sigmundr are Vǫlsungr and Hljóð’s eldest children and twins.
Signý’s honey stratagem enables Sigmundr to kill the she-wolf and escape the stocks.

relations.myth: Signý conceives Sinfjǫtli in magical disguise
relations.note: Disguised as another woman, Signý sleeps with her unwitting twin for three nights.
Signý conceals Sigmundr’s sword in straw, enabling him and Sinfjǫtli to escape burial.
Signý preserves and assists Sigmundr throughout their long campaign against Siggeirr.
Signý is unwillingly married to Siggeirr, king of Gautland.

relations.myth: Signý exchanges appearances with a sorceress
relations.note: Signý substitutes a disguised sorceress in Siggeirr’s bed without his knowledge.

relations.myth: Vengeance and the burning of Siggeirr’s hall
relations.note: Signý engineers the revenge culminating in Siggeirr’s death when his hall is burned.
Signý bears Sinfjǫtli after conceiving him with her twin brother Sigmundr.
Signý tests Sinfjǫtli, sends him to Sigmundr, and employs him as her avenger.
Sigurðr is Signý’s nephew through Sigmundr and is born after her death.
Helgi is Signý’s nephew through Sigmundr; no direct interaction is recorded.
Hámundr is Signý’s nephew through Sigmundr; no direct interaction is recorded.
